scope: Consolidated cross-level review proposal. No alias is applied or exported to runtime. Source cards and CEFR labels are unchanged. No new independent CEFR verification.

policy.base_fields: Use unchanged lower-level ID, headword, definitions, translations, forms, and notes. Keep all B1 content in separately labeled variants, with each example, translation and grammar tied to its own meaning.
policy.variant_resolution: Use the numbered report and report_row to read b1.record. If variant_source is present, overlay any explicitly curated usage-variant fields from the same report and matching B1 ID. Keep b1.record as provenance. Report files are pinned to source_commit.
policy.release: Resolve source report follow-up items and independently confirm CEFR scope, then test display, search, practice, and ID-based progress before applying. Keep legacy IDs as pending references and preserve independent practice for constructions.
policy.duplicate_b1: B1 stages remain authoritative for intra-B1 relations. Both variants of kosten meaning taste stay independent from the price card. Both B1 telefonieren uses point to the same A1 target, with both source IDs and distinct learning contexts reserved. Same-ID physical duplicate rows in intra-B1 review do not create further aliases.

decisions.reason: The A2 note explicitly includes neben + Akkusativ for a destination; keep the Dativ position and Akkusativ destination examples separate.
Schwere Arbeit describes difficult or strenuous work. The physical-weight card is the wrong target.
The A2 definition and its Tasche example explicitly cover carrying an object.
Kosten tragen means bear or pay the costs. This is independent of physically carrying or wearing.
A dream during sleep differs from an aspiration. The lower card defines only the aspiration.
Traurig about an ending expresses something that causes sadness. The lower definition covers feeling sadness.
Keep the no-precipitation weather gloss separately from the physical dryness example.
Both records describe being in love with someone and use in + Akkusativ.
Losing keys matches the lower example about losing a hat.
The definition includes no longer having something; preserve losing a job with its own Russian gloss.
